newsitem.title: JAPAN: JAPAN MOF, INSURERS AGREE ON SCHEME FOR NISSAN LIFE.
newsitem.headline: JAPAN MOF, INSURERS AGREE ON SCHEME FOR NISSAN LIFE.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance and a life insurance group have hammered out a framework to deal with huge losses at failed Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co, industry sources said on Wednesday.
Under the scheme, a new company will be set up jointly by life insurers to liquidate the failed insurer, taking over its policies and managing them until they mature, they said.
The Finance Ministry ordered Nissan Life to shut down its operations on April 25, marking the first failure of a life insurance firm in post-war Japan.

The insurer's actual liabilities exceed its assets by around 300 billion yen, and the Policyholders Protection Fund, comprised of contributions from life insurers, will inject 200 billion yen into the new company.
The remaining 100 billion yen in liabilities will be transferred to the new company, which is to cover the losses through its profits over a period of five years, sources said.
The framework is expected to be unveiled on Friday at a news conference by the Life Insurance Association of Japan, they said.
They added, however, that there is no guarantee that the new company will be profitable enough to cover the 100 billion yen in losses in the mandated five-year period.
And if it cannot cover the losses, it has not yet been decided who would shoulder the burden: policyholders, the industry or the government.
Despite such lingering uncertainties, the industry and the Finance Ministry, eager to restore faith among policyholders, decided to go ahead with the announcement of the framework.

"The ministry and the association wanted to draw up a framework by the end of this month, as they felt a need to try to prevent (life insurance) policyholders' confidence in the industry from diminishing," an industry source said.

The Life Insurance Association, serving as an interim caretaker for Nissan Life since its failure, has found it a perplexing task to draw up the framework as no candidates have come forward prepared to take over Nissan Life's policies.

Nissan Life's major clients, Hitachi Ltd and Nissan Motor Co Ltd, rejected a request by the association to aid Nissan Life, and no major life insurer has been willing to take over the failed company's policies.
Nissan Life suffered heavy losses through excessive stock and real estate investments in the late 1980s "bubble era" of inflated asset prices.
In addition, nearly half of Nissan Life's assets are individual pension policies guaranteeing high returns. Those commitments have also damaged the company's financial stability.
The sources said the new company taking over Nissan Life's assets would probably ask policyholders to accept a reduction in the high returns they have enjoyed.

They added that the company will impose penalties if policyholders cancel their contracts with Nissan Life and will halt dividend payments during the five-year period in order to boost profits and help cover the losses.
The sources also said that Nissan Life's workers would probably be dismissed and only a few of them would be rehired by the new company, in a bid to cut costs.

The daily Asahi Shimbun newspaper reported that if the framework is approved at Nissan Life's policyholders' meeting at the end of July, the company will be liquidated and policies will be transferred to the new company in August.
The financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said the new company to be set up to liquidate Nissan Life would also take up the role of handling any failures that may occur at other life insurers.
